summary: The note surveys school safety and bullying prevention initiatives across several districts, covering security measures, empathy curricula, community involvement, educator training, reporting technology and support for vulnerable groups. It cites a statistic that nearly one in three students has experienced bullying and stresses that safety is a shared responsibility of schools, families and communities. It closes by calling for ongoing adaptation and commitment from all stakeholders.
one_line: Overview of school safety and anti-bullying initiatives across districts, from security systems and empathy curricula to community partnerships, training and reporting apps.
key_facts: Reports published in late September say nearly one in three students has experienced bullying at some point in their academic life.
In October 2023, Dr. Maria Gonzales, Superintendent of the East Valley School District, launched the "Fortress of Learning" initiative.
The "Fortress of Learning" program combines state-of-the-art surveillance systems, stringent access controls, and faculty training to detect and deescalate threats.
Hamilton Middle School Principal James O'Reilly has led a district-wide digital citizenship campaign starting November 2, 2023, to address cyberbullying.
Elementary schools in the Springfield School District adopted the "Kindness Counts" curriculum starting January 15, teaching empathy, inclusion, and the consequences of bullying.
Lincoln Elementary is cited as a school integrating discussions of emotions, respect and harassment into daily classroom activities.
On February 20, community leader Andre Thompson and the local police department held a town hall meeting in Brooksville on community's role in school safety.
The Brooksville forum led to a partnership of local businesses, parents and the education system and a collaborative funding effort for school safety improvements.

The Jefferson County School Board, led by Chairman William Hayes, started an educator training program on March 12 covering identifying bullying, defusing violence, and supporting victims, including psychological first-aid.
The "SafeVoice" app, developed by a startup, was rolled out district-wide in Riverview on April 1 and lets students anonymously report bullying or safety concerns via smartphone.
The Unity and Respect Initiative, starting May 3 in the Midtown School District, offers workshops, mentorship and resource centers for marginalized students.
LGBTQ+ youth, students with disabilities, and students from minority ethnic backgrounds are described as facing heightened targeted violence and discrimination.
